identity.title: History
identity.subtitle: The human past is too large for one path. Read it by time, by place, or by a recurring theme—then combine the lenses to explain how change happened.

organization.title: One history. Three coordinate systems.
organization.description: Each lens keeps different relationships visible. None is complete alone, and none is merely a different menu for the same list.

items.label: History by Time
items.question: When?
items.summary: Follow sequence, duration, turning points, change, and continuity from deep human history to the present.

items.label: History by Place
items.question: Where?
items.summary: Compare local experiences and trace the movement of people, goods, ideas, institutions, and environments across regions.

items.label: History by Theme
items.question: What pattern?
items.summary: Follow power, exchange, belief, technology, health, environment, and everyday life across many eras and places.

sections.title: The printing press is not only a date.
sections.summary: A historical explanation gets stronger when the same development is located in sequence, geography, and recurring human systems.

columns.label: Time
columns.question: What changed before and after print became widespread?
columns.answer: Compare manuscript culture, expanding print networks, and later mass publishing.

columns.label: Place
columns.question: Where did presses, books, and literacy move?
columns.answer: Trace cities, trade routes, language regions, states, and the uneven reach of print.

columns.label: Theme
columns.question: Which systems did print reshape?
columns.answer: Follow effects on religion, politics, education, commerce, science, and public debate.
